text:
mei: Quick heads-up — while bringing up nova-v2 (int6) on cn-onboard we see a weird cascade where whole sinogram clusters get split and then sometimes collapse to punctuation. Examples below.
ryan: Can you paste a minimal prompt + outputs? quick snippet will do.
mei: Sample (short):
```
src: 我去北京大学。
ref: I went to Peking University.
int6: 我 去 北京 大学 。
float: 我去北京大学。
```
mei: More worrying: in longer contexts the sinogram span becomes `... 。` (single punctuation) mid-sentence after a few tokens. Seems like multi-token collapse.
anya: :eyes: that's alarming. Any eval numbers?
eval-bot: Automated eval: zh-en BLEU delta = -4.3 on cn-eval-5k; sinogram-cluster token-accuracy down 18% vs float32 baseline. Regression flagged.
tomo: Which quant toolchain/config? q-optimizer? per-channel vs per-tensor? kernel runtime?
mei: Repro notes: quantize with qopt v0.3 --bits=6 --per-channel; runtime=v2-kernel-xla with continuous-batching enabled. Dataset: cn-onboard-100k (sampled).
ryan: Could be tokenization mapping changes during export -> token ids shift and then quant noise amplifies it. Any detok differences?
mei: I ran detok compare: most cases detok matches, but for clustered sinograms the token boundaries differ (split vs unsplit) between int6 and float. Combined with lower logits margin, generation falls back to punctuation.
anya: Action items: repro on int8 (control), run with per-row quant, and check export stubs (tokenmap). Assign?
ryan: assigning to @tomo and tagging @infra for canary runs. Please create a ticket.
tomo: On it. I'll run int8 vs int6 per-channel/per-row today and attach nbest logits for affected spans.
mei: I'll upload artifact (samples + eval) to the run link: https://redwood.internal/run/1234 (internal).
ryan: Also ask devex to spin tokenizer variant cn-sinogram-v2 to compare mapping.
mei: My suspicion: quantization noise + kernel selection changes KV-cache alignment for multi-byte sinogram clusters -> early termination/punctuation spike.
ryan: Good hypothesis. If true, mitigation options: stronger bias correction during quant, or fallback to int8 for locale-sensitive routes.
anya: +1. If canary reproduces, plan a quick canary rollback for cn region traffic.
infra-bot: Ticket RED-ML-2348 created by ryan: "nova-v2 int6 sinogram cascade token loss".
mei: I'll paste a minimal repro script and a couple more examples in the ticket in ~30m.
